dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The supplied publishing gist and interview identify Nick's need to turn his own perspective into useful buyer-facing articles without losing authorship, inventing evidence, or manually coordinating every agent activity.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Nick selected an end-to-end first Admin publishing surface, full editable archive migration, a $5 automatic allowance per publishing attempt, three mandatory approvals, and a three-piece editorial pilot.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Nick explicitly accepted automated safety and migration checks, desktop/mobile task review, a three-piece owner-reviewed pilot, and build/lint/static-analysis checks; business inquiries are a later outcome rather than a launch promise.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: The interview includes Composer capture, an Ideas/Active writing dashboard, an extended Flux manuscript editor, the entire archive, bounded assistance and publication; discovery automation, image generation, distribution, learning and MCP access are deferred.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: Nick approved the browser-tested Flux custom-block approach, distinguished Composer idea entry from manuscript editing, retained explicit human gates and live-version isolation, and rejected a mandatory ZDR routing requirement.

problem: Birdcar needs a personal editorial power tool, not an autonomous content factory. Nick supplies the perspective and makes editorial decisions; agents develop the opportunity, ask questions, retrieve evidence, organize arguments, draft, review and prepare a release. The present application has no Admin UI or persistent publishing workflow: its Admin index is a permission-gated empty response and its ten-essay archive is read from Markdown files.

The first Admin surface must make the work approachable: a Flux Composer accepts a simple idea, an Ideas/Active writing dashboard separates the backlog from deliberate work, and a quiet manuscript editor carries prose and meaningful content blocks. Existing authorization, public-route boundaries and offer truth are foundations to reuse, not reasons to preserve the file-backed publishing architecture.

The business outcome is qualified service inquiries from relevant owners and operational leaders. Articles should help them recognize a problem, trust Nick's judgment, and understand when the pitch-free Walkthrough is useful. Neither traffic nor this implementation proves attribution or lead quality. No productivity baseline or model-quality benchmark has been established.
goals: Deliver the first usable Admin publishing workspace: submit an idea, develop it with agents, make the three human decisions, edit and review the manuscript, then publish or schedule an exact approved release without leaving the application.

Make every essay in the initial ten-article archive editable in the CMS while preserving its public prose, title, original date, URL, links, chart data and diagram meaning; keep original source files intact as migration evidence.

Keep Nick in control: agents advance only within an authorized stage, changes to human prose remain proposals, stale work cannot overwrite newer work, and a published release stays live while a replacement is developed.

Bound automatic work to a $5 allowance per publishing attempt, including model calls, research tools and retries; permit one three-lens review batch and one affected-area recheck before further work requires a deliberate human restart or allowance increase.

Complete a three-piece pilot covering an opinion-led piece, a practical explanation and an evidence-heavy article, with Nick approving voice and reader usefulness, all material factual/publication blockers resolved, and editing time, retained prose and actual spending recorded.

successCriteria.criterion: Editorial transitions enforce angle approval before research/outline generation, plan approval before full drafting, and exact-release approval before publication. Missing answers, park/abandon actions and unresolved blocking findings prevent inappropriate advancement. Imported published articles do not require retrospective approval of their historical creation.

check.expect: Exits 0 with allowed and denied transition tests, pause/resume behavior and imported-article revision coverage.

successCriteria.criterion: Publication and scheduling use the approved immutable release, never the latest working document. Editing approved release content invalidates its approval and withdraws its schedule; editing a published article leaves the live version unchanged. Duplicate delivery and stale worker results cannot double-publish or overwrite newer state.

check.expect: Exits 0 with stale approval, concurrent edit, schedule withdrawal, duplicate delivery and live-version isolation cases.

successCriteria.criterion: A publishing attempt starts with a $5 automatic allowance that is not reset by autosaves or generated revisions. Parallel work and retries reserve their maximum authorized cost before dispatch; unpriced or unaffordable work pauses. Actual usage is reconciled and a top-up requires a human action. This is application-side preauthorization, not a guarantee about a provider's invoice.

check.expect: Exits 0 with simultaneous reservations, insufficient balance, missing prices, retry spending, unknown usage and explicit top-up coverage using fake providers.

successCriteria.criterion: Research retains actual retrieved supporting passages, source URLs and retrieval dates, distinguishes supplied recollection/interpretation from external fact, and marks missing or contradictory evidence for resolution. External text cannot grant tool authority; unsafe fetch destinations are denied. AI-use consent does not imply permission to publish client details.

check.expect: Exits 0 with retrieved-evidence, missing-source, contradictory-source, malicious-source-instruction, unsafe-fetch and publication-permission scenarios; no real external requests occur.

successCriteria.criterion: Facts/argument, voice/narrative and buyer/discovery reviews inspect the same revision, return passage-specific findings rather than overwriting the manuscript, and reconcile duplicate/conflicting advice for the owner. Accepted changes preserve protected human passages and reject stale proposals. Only one automatic affected-area recheck follows the initial batch.

check.expect: Exits 0 with no-change results, conflicting findings, accepted/rejected proposals, protected passages, stale results and exhausted-cycle coverage.

successCriteria.criterion: The archive importer is repeatable without duplicate articles or overwriting later CMS edits. Every original archive entry retains its identity, text, dates, links and structured figure data. Original resources/writing files remain byte-identical to the pre-project source baseline. Public Writing, individual articles, RSS, sitemap and canonical metadata read only published CMS releases after cutover.

check.cmd: php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/Publishing/ArchiveMigrationTest.php tests/Feature/MarketingSiteTest.php tests/Feature/MarketingDiagramTest.php tests/Feature/MarketingDiscoveryTest.php && git diff --exit-code 72f7d8ad8521573cb224022c902447f9ca4c4351 -- resources/writing
check.expect: Exits 0 with baseline-archive parity, repeat-import safety and public unpublished-content denial; original source files still match the pinned pre-project baseline even after implementation commits. Existing public assertions remain meaningful rather than being weakened to accommodate losses.

successCriteria.criterion: The production document model preserves supported prose, links, notes, callouts, chart values/captions and editable diagram definitions through save/load. Unsupported nodes, unsafe URLs and executable markup cannot enter public rendering; invalid chart values or diagram source produce actionable validation errors, not partial publication.

check.expect: Exits 0 with document round trips, all supported block types, hostile/unsupported content and failed-save non-mutation cases. Real browser editor behavior is additionally reviewed below.

successCriteria.criterion: Admin admission continues to use admin.view, while every publishing mutation checks a transport-neutral publishing capability. Unauthenticated users, users with admission only, and unrelated organization memberships cannot read or mutate protected editorial content through routes or Livewire actions.

check.expect: Exits 0 with positive role-based grants, admission-only denial and direct-action denial; definitions use the existing Catalog and authorization:sync conventions.

successCriteria.criterion: The application builds and passes its configured formatting and static-analysis checks with the production editor integration and all required publishing tests present. Skipped and incomplete Publishing tests fail acceptance.

check.cmd: bun run build && bun test resources/js/admin/publishing/document-helpers.test.js && composer lint:check && composer types:check && vendor/bin/pest --compact --fail-on-skipped --fail-on-incomplete tests/Feature/Publishing tests/Feature/Auth/AdminFortifyFlowTest.php
check.expect: Every command exits 0; required feature-test files are exercised by the other named checks, and any skipped or incomplete Publishing test produces a nonzero exit code.

successCriteria.criterion: The migrated archive preserves rendered meaning, not merely imported bytes: original notes, links, chart labels/values, diagrams and captions remain understandable on desktop, mobile, with JavaScript disabled, and in print.

check.judgment: Nick reviews representative rendered archive cases alongside the originals at desktop/mobile widths and in no-JavaScript/print output; approve only when no original meaning, text or link destination is lost.

successCriteria.criterion: The Admin workspace supports the agreed task journey: Composer submission starts development, Save for later stays passive, Ideas and Active writing remain distinct, Published is separate, and the rich editor supports block changes, saving/reloading, review decisions and release confirmation without losing work.

check.judgment: Nick performs the named journey on desktop and mobile with keyboard-accessible controls, including a failed save/retry and a stale edit conflict, and explicitly accepts the interaction; automated feature tests cover the underlying state changes.

successCriteria.criterion: The three representative pilot pieces are publishable in Nick's judgment: each preserves his actual viewpoint, has no unresolved invented experience or material factual/rights issue, and serves its approved reader. Editorial effort, retained first-draft prose and actual model/tool spend are recorded without asserting an unmeasured time saving or business conversion lift.

check.judgment: Nick reviews all three final manuscripts against their approved briefs, supporting evidence and chosen voice samples; explicitly accepts or rejects each on viewpoint, rhythm, specificity, rhetorical restraint and reader usefulness, and reviews the recorded effort/cost observations.

mvp.item: First Admin shell and usable sign-in path, reusing Fortify, standard Admin routes, existing global identity and domain-local permission catalogs; Flux UI Pro with Inter.
mvp.reason: The repository currently has no usable Admin UI. Publishing must have real authenticated entry and action-level authorization, including an explicit operator procedure to provision Nick's confirmed existing account with the catalog-defined Admin and publishing roles, without building a general administration suite.

mvp.item: Flux Composer idea entry with Develop idea and Save for later; Ideas/Active writing dashboard, attention indicators and a separate published archive.
mvp.reason: Nick explicitly selected this composition and clarified that submitting the simple idea should initiate agent-assisted development.

mvp.item: One Flux rich-text manuscript editor with Markdown shortcuts, custom semantic notes/callouts/charts/diagrams, contextual block controls and a real public-article preview.
mvp.reason: Nick approved this approach after a disposable prototype proved representative block edits and exact structured-document persistence across a full browser reload.

mvp.item: Persistent editorial state, working revisions, save/conflict handling, protected human passages, explicit alternatives and immutable approved/live releases.
mvp.reason: Agents, delayed jobs and human edits must not silently replace one another or publish unapproved material.

mvp.item: Full migration of the original archive into editable CMS records, preserving original files as evidence and all public content identities and meaning.
mvp.reason: Nick rejected a read-only legacy archive and on-demand migration; the first release must edit the whole archive.

mvp.item: Agent-assisted interview/brief, human angle approval, live public-source research and challenge, narrative/outline and visual planning, human plan approval, and drafting from approved context.
mvp.reason: The first useful release must complete the editorial journey, not ship a manual editor awaiting its intelligence.

mvp.item: Small explicit editorial roles using OpenRouter, relevant voice examples separate from business truth and evidence, usage accounting, a $5 per-attempt allowance and bounded retry/pause behavior.
mvp.reason: The tool must preserve authorship and control costs without a generic agent platform, model registry or automatically learned voice profile.

mvp.item: Three same-revision review lenses, reconciled passage-specific proposals, explicit human dispositions, one targeted recheck, and publication-blocking factual/safety findings distinct from advisory style/discovery suggestions.
mvp.reason: This is the approved review authority and stopping rule; model agreement is not proof and reviewers cannot independently overwrite prose.

mvp.item: Purposeful structured visuals, release metadata/link/asset checks, exact-release approval, publish/schedule, and safe replacement of public Writing/RSS/sitemap content.
mvp.reason: A usable publishing product must deliver the approved release, not stop at generating a draft. New diagrams use editable source plus preview rather than a visual drawing application.

mvp.item: Owner-reviewed three-piece pilot and explicit acceptance gate, plus focused automated regressions and rendered archive/desktop/mobile review.
mvp.reason: Passing tests does not establish voice fidelity, editorial usefulness or a usable writing interaction; no existing performance baseline is invented.

future: Agent-discovered opportunities and measured buyer demand.
Generated illustrations, richer media handling and distribution drafts.
Outcome-informed recommendations and owner-approved reusable voice/editorial learning.
A separate Admin MCP interface reusing the same capabilities and transition rules.
More content-type-specific review presets after the initial substantial-article pilot.

decisions.decision: Require separate angle, plan and exact-release approval for new pieces.
decisions.rejected: Combining brief/outline into a single early approval gate.
decisions.reason: Nick explicitly preferred control before both research effort and full drafting.

decisions.decision: Plan the editorial process together with the first Admin dashboard and writing workspace.
decisions.rejected: Ending this project at a process-only design document.
decisions.reason: Nick expanded the initial gist boundary to include the first Admin UI, using Flux UI Pro and existing permissions.

decisions.decision: Deliver an assisted end-to-end first release while deferring discovery automation, generated images, distribution, learning and MCP.
decisions.rejected: The entire long-term vision at once, or a manual workspace with agents added later.
decisions.reason: Nick selected the working editorial journey as the minimum useful product.

decisions.decision: Use Ideas plus Active writing on the landing dashboard, with Published separate.
decisions.rejected: Ideas plus Published as the primary split, or a decisions-first landing dashboard.
decisions.reason: Nick selected a creation-focused workspace rather than leading with past output or a queue of administrative decisions.

decisions.decision: Agents advance within the authorized stage and stop at human decisions, missing input and budget limits.
decisions.rejected: Requiring a separate instruction or estimate approval for every agent activity.
decisions.reason: Nick wants agents to start and advance useful work, not merely expose a set of manual AI buttons.

decisions.decision: Use rich text with Markdown shortcuts for the manuscript.
decisions.rejected: Markdown-source editing or interchangeable rich-text/Markdown editing modes.
decisions.reason: Nick selected a quiet rendered writing surface; source-format round trips are not a product requirement.

decisions.decision: Make the entire existing essay archive editable in the first release.
decisions.rejected: Keeping legacy essays read-only or importing them only when individually revised.
decisions.reason: Nick explicitly requires one CMS for old and new writing, with public fidelity preserved.

decisions.decision: Run one three-lens batch and one affected-area recheck after accepted revisions.
decisions.rejected: Two automatic revision cycles or recurring manual selection of every review.
decisions.reason: The chosen default provides useful specialist feedback without an endless refinement loop.

decisions.decision: Use a $5 automatic allowance per publishing attempt, spanning autosaves, generated revisions and retries.
decisions.rejected: A $2 allowance or approval of every stage estimate.
decisions.reason: Nick chose more room for meaningful research/escalation, while retaining an explicit stop and top-up decision.

decisions.decision: Use a three-piece editorial pilot without an invented manual-work baseline.
decisions.rejected: A single-piece acceptance pilot or an unmeasured time-savings promise.
decisions.reason: Nick selected representative opinion, practical and evidence-heavy writing with measured observations and his own editorial judgment.

decisions.decision: Use structured editorial blocks and source-based diagram authoring.
decisions.rejected: Read-only figures or a full point-and-click diagram/chart design application.
decisions.reason: Nick wants content to remain editable without making the CMS a general-purpose visual-design tool.

decisions.decision: Material factual, invented-detail, confidentiality/rights and release-integrity issues block publication; style/discovery suggestions are advisory.
decisions.rejected: Blanket editorial overrides for unresolved factual/rights issues, or requiring every advisory finding to be cleared.
decisions.reason: Flags can be resolved by evidence, revision/removal or a reasoned false-positive disposition; reviewers advise rather than acquire editorial veto authority.

decisions.decision: Keep AI processing and publication permission distinct, without requiring ZDR-only providers.
decisions.rejected: Mandatory zero-retention provider routes for this personal publishing workflow.
decisions.reason: Nick clarified that he does not generally handle confidential material and will disclose AI use contractually. An explicitly marked private source still needs deliberate processing consent and separate permission to disclose its contents.

decisions.decision: Use documented Flux custom Tiptap extensions for one continuous manuscript editor, with contextual block controls.
decisions.rejected: Assuming stock Flux preserves custom figures, or splitting the manuscript into separate prose editors solely to avoid extensions.
decisions.reason: Boost's Flux 2 documentation confirms registerExtensions/init support. The 2026-09-22 disposable spike using installed Flux 2.19 and temporary Tiptap 2.11.7 retained two notes/callouts, chart data, a diagram and a link after edits and full browser reload; stock Flux dropped the figure nodes. It also exposed the need to isolate embedded-figure whitespace/typography. The temporary sandbox is evidence, not a runtime dependency or production implementation.

decisions.decision: Use Flux Composer for initial idea entry; submitting Develop idea is explicit authorization to start the interview/brief, while Save for later is passive.
decisions.rejected: Using the manuscript editor or a large article form as the initial idea input.
decisions.reason: Nick clarified that he is logging a simple idea and letting an agent start a process. This preserves deliberate initiation without making capture cumbersome.

decisions.decision: Separate automated safety checks from owner editorial/usability acceptance and later business outcomes.
decisions.rejected: Treating green tests as voice approval or requiring a speculative conversion lift before launch.
decisions.reason: Nick explicitly accepted the proposed acceptance checks; existing ideation learnings also warn that markup/build checks do not prove rendered behavior or human judgment.

decisions.decision: Include an explicit owner-account provisioning prerequisite using authorization:sync and domain-local role assignments before the real Admin pilot.
decisions.rejected: Assuming that installing authorization or seeding a User already grants Nick Admin and publishing access.
decisions.reason: The hidden-dependency critic verified that the repository has no owner-role provisioning path. The implementation spec must identify an owner-confirmed existing account, require authorization for privileged assignments, assign roles rather than direct permissions, and never grant access from boot or migrations.

decisions.decision: Mechanically compare original archive sources with the pinned pre-project Git baseline in addition to imported/rendered parity tests.
decisions.rejected: Relying on public-content parity tests, or a clean working-tree diff alone, to prove the original source files were not rewritten.
decisions.reason: The success-criteria critic exposed missing source-preservation coverage. Comparing against commit 72f7d8ad8521573cb224022c902447f9ca4c4351 detects source changes even after they have been committed.

decisions.decision: Fail acceptance on skipped or incomplete Publishing tests using supported Pest runner flags.
decisions.rejected: Assuming a normal green test-run exit code guarantees that all Publishing tests actually ran.
decisions.reason: The success-criteria critic noted that skipped tests may otherwise pass; the installed runner confirms --fail-on-skipped and --fail-on-incomplete support.

decisions.decision: Register Admin application routes explicitly in routes/web.php; reserve Folio for the marketing site.
decisions.rejected: Using file-based Folio routing for the authenticated publishing application.
decisions.reason: Nick explicitly reinforced this boundary after contract approval; it also matches the existing committed application-routing rule. Livewire components do not imply Folio routes.

decisions.decision: Build a shared Admin shell and explicit module route/navigation boundaries, with publishing as its first module.
decisions.rejected: Coupling the whole Admin layout and navigation to publishing, or prebuilding a generic module/plugin framework.
decisions.reason: Nick expects substantial future Admin functionality. Reusable Flux/Inter layout, navigation and feedback patterns earn their place now; future module features, dynamic registries and permission-management UI remain out of scope.

decisions.decision: Use Tiptap-compatible canonical JSON with server-side typed rendering, and restricted static SVG source for new diagrams.
decisions.rejected: A parallel incompatible document AST, HTML as authoritative persistence, or additional diagram-rendering infrastructure.
decisions.reason: Spec integration review aligned server node names/attrs with the approved editor and retained source-plus-preview authoring without a new drawing or runtime dependency. Original prose and figures remain protected by independent migration parity checks.

decisions.decision: Implement OpenRouter through Laravel HTTP, using an explicit Exa web plugin, stored retrieved highlights and safe public fetch where supporting text is absent.
decisions.rejected: Adding an AI SDK, implicit search-engine/provider fallback, or treating citation URLs alone as supporting evidence.
decisions.reason: Current official OpenRouter documentation supplies a concrete one-vendor integration. Search and model charges remain inside pre-call reservations; uncertain prices/outcomes pause. Model/provider choices and paid calls stay owner-controlled execution inputs.

decisions.decision: Approve production installation of exactly @tiptap/core@2.11.7 and @tiptap/pm@2.11.7, including package.json and bun.lock updates.
decisions.rejected: Stopping after backend phases or deferring all implementation because editor dependency approval was still pending.
decisions.reason: Nick explicitly approved these two tested packages in the execution-time dependency gate. This authorization does not extend to additional packages, paid model calls, credentials, privileged account changes or deployment.

decisions.decision: Commit environment guidance and planning artifacts separately, then let the watched engine commit each phase after passing tests and code review without additional message prompts.
decisions.rejected: Mixing unrelated environment guidance into feature commits or requiring repeated commit-message approvals during the already-approved express build.
decisions.reason: Nick explicitly approved both initial commit messages and subsequent tested/reviewed conventional phase commits. Include the exact phase spec path in each phase commit body, never add Co-Authored-By trailers, and retain interactive failure and authorization gates.

execution.strategy: Sequential execution of five build phases on the express isolation branch, followed by an explicit owner acceptance gate. All agreed first-release items are MVP, with no additional Full or Stretch scope. The owner approved express generation and watched execution; specs now exist. The kind=gate phase is a human checklist, excluded from unattended build/commit dispatch and never counted as automatically accepted.

phases.title: Publishing foundation and release integrity
phases.notes: Define the concrete publishing domain, approvals, revisions/releases, pause/park/abandon behavior, publishing-attempt budget identity and publishing capabilities using existing authorization catalogs. Add EditorialWorkflowTest.php, ReleaseIntegrityTest.php and PublishingAuthorizationTest.php under tests/Feature/Publishing; these are planned deliverables, not pre-existing files. Reuse the single User identity; no tenant publishing or generic workflow engine. Specify the operator bootstrap: run authorization:sync, identify Nick's existing account with his confirmation, then explicitly authorize and assign catalog-defined Admin and publishing roles; never infer a target email, assign direct permissions, grant access in boot/migrations, or create an account without approval.

phases.title: Structured documents and archive import
phases.notes: Implement production document validation/rendering, supported semantic blocks, editable diagram source with deterministic static output, and a repeatable archive importer. Preserve original source files; imported content becomes an initial published snapshot, with future edits in a working revision. Add DocumentRoundTripTest.php and ArchiveMigrationTest.php. Re-prove Flux extension/save-load behavior in production code rather than depending on the temporary sandbox. Name and seek explicit approval for any production editor/diagram/sanitization dependencies before installation. Public-reader cutover follows only after parity and release delivery are ready.

phases.title: First Admin publishing workspace
phases.notes: Provide a usable existing-account sign-in/logout path through Fortify, a reusable Flux/Inter Admin shell with module-aware navigation and shared feedback patterns, explicit standard routes in routes/web.php with a routes/admin.php module entry point, Composer idea entry, Ideas/Active writing, Published archive, the continuous editor, contextual block editing, public preview, visible save/conflict states and approval/review surfaces. Extend action-level tests with workspace feature coverage. No account-management suite, tenant UI, marketing redesign or placeholder analytics dashboard.

phases.title: Agent development, evidence and bounded reviews
phases.notes: Wire explicit queued editorial activities to OpenRouter and actual public-source search/fetch, three human gates and same-revision review proposals. Add AgentBudgetTest.php, EvidenceResearchTest.php and EditorialReviewTest.php. Implement reservations, bounded retries, stale-result rejection and durable pause/resume; use existing Laravel facilities rather than a general agent framework. Specify the concrete search/fetch integration, required credentials, external data flow and usage pricing before real calls. The gist's model/provider IDs and prices are evaluation hypotheses and must be revalidated. No laravel/ai dependency is installed today; any SDK addition needs explicit approval. Fake all external calls during automated development; no credentials or paid calls are assumed available.

phases.title: Release delivery and public cutover
prereqs: Agent development, evidence and bounded reviews
phases.notes: Complete release packaging, material-blocker resolution, deterministic publish/schedule delivery and CMS-backed public Writing/RSS/sitemap reads. Cut over only after archive parity passes and preserve existing public SEO, rendering and route boundaries. Exercise retries, schedule withdrawal and live-version isolation; run affected public tests and configured code-quality checks. Document the local cutover/recovery procedure in the implementation spec; production deployment remains a separately authorized action.

phases.title: Owner editorial and usability acceptance
phases.notes: Human checkpoint, not unattended proof of completion. Before the pilot, the operator completes the documented authorization:sync and approved role-provisioning procedure for Nick's confirmed existing account and verifies sign-in. Nick authorizes/configures real provider credentials and paid pilot work, reviews public archive fidelity and desktop/mobile workflow, then accepts or rejects the three representative manuscripts with effort/cost observations. Agent code review, successful tests or automatic verification cannot grant this approval or authorize production deployment.
